en: The amount of something, such as energy or food, that people use or buy; or the act of using it.
ex: The car has low fuel consumption.
這輛車的油耗很低。

en: The movement of people or goods from one place to another; or the passing through a place.
ex: The package was lost in transit.
包裹在運送途中遺失了。

en: The act of keeping things in a place until they are needed; or the space used for this.
ex: We put the old furniture into storage.
我們把舊家具放進倉庫儲存。

en: Easily harmed, attacked or influenced.
ex: Elderly people are particularly vulnerable to the flu.
老年人特別容易感染流感。

en: To experience something unpleasant or a big change.
ex: The patient will undergo surgery tomorrow morning.
病人明天早上要接受手術。

en: To make someone believe something that is not true.
ex: He deceived her into giving him all her savings.
他騙她把所有積蓄都交給他。

en: A dish of meat or vegetables cooked slowly in liquid; or to cook food in this way.
ex: She made a hearty beef stew for dinner.
她煮了一鍋豐盛的燉牛肉當晚餐。

en: To be careful about something dangerous or unpleasant.
ex: Beware of pickpockets in crowded areas.
在擁擠的地方要小心扒手。

en: To harm someone who trusts you by breaking a promise or secretly helping their enemy.
ex: He betrayed his friends by telling the police their secret.
他向警方洩露了朋友的祕密而背叛了他們。

en: Similar in size, quality or amount, so that you can compare them.
ex: His salary is comparable to that of a doctor.
他的薪水與醫生相當。

en: Following one after another without a break.
ex: The team has won five consecutive games.
這支球隊已連續贏了五場比賽。

en: A metal bar that slides across to fasten a door; or to run away suddenly.
ex: She bolted the door and went to bed.
她閂上門後就去睡了。

en: To gradually make something weaker or less effective.
ex: Constant criticism can undermine a child's confidence.
不斷的批評會削弱孩子的信心。

en: To officially change a law or document; or to improve something.
ex: Congress voted to amend the law.
國會投票修改該法律。

en: To agree to give or allow something; or an amount of money given by an organization for a purpose.
ex: The university gave her a grant to fund her research.
大學給了她一筆補助款來資助研究。

en: To go into or through something, especially when it is difficult.
ex: The bullet penetrated the wall.
子彈穿透了牆壁。

en: The money used in a particular country; or the state of being widely used or known.
ex: You can exchange your dollars for the local currency here.
你可以在這裡把美元兌換成當地貨幣。

en: A long narrow passage in a building with doors on either side; or a strip of land.
ex: The classrooms are all along the same corridor.
教室都在同一條走廊上。

en: Containing poison and able to cause illness or death.
ex: The factory released toxic chemicals into the river.
這家工廠把有毒化學物質排入河中。

en: The regular beat of blood in your arteries; or to beat or move with a strong, regular rhythm.
ex: The nurse checked the patient's pulse.
護理師檢查了病人的脈搏。

en: Easy to see or realize; clear and obvious.
ex: There has been a noticeable improvement in his grades.
他的成績有了明顯的進步。

en: Causing great damage or harm.
ex: The hurricane was one of the most destructive in history.
這場颶風是歷史上破壞力最強的颶風之一。

en: A suggestion about the best thing to do; or a letter praising someone for a job.
ex: I got the job on the recommendation of my teacher.
我是靠老師的推薦得到這份工作的。

en: Relating to the way something is built or organized.
ex: The earthquake caused serious structural damage to the building.
地震對這棟建築造成嚴重的結構性損壞。

en: A frame or shelf for holding things; or to cause someone great pain or worry.
ex: He put his bag on the rack above his seat.
他把包包放在座位上方的行李架上。

en: A very small part of something; or a number written as one number over another.
ex: The new model costs only a fraction of the old price.
新型號只需舊價格的一小部分。

en: A large container with a handle and a lip used for pouring; or the player who throws the ball in baseball.
ex: She filled a pitcher with iced tea.
她用冰茶裝滿了一壺。

en: A long pipe that carries oil or gas; or a system through which things are passed or developed.
ex: New products are in the pipeline for next year.
明年有新產品在籌備中。

en: To push someone or something roughly; or a rough push.
ex: He shoved the door open with his shoulder.
他用肩膀把門撞開。

en: The ability to do something well or to a good standard.
ex: The job requires a high level of technical competence.
這份工作需要很高的技術能力。

en: Coming after something in time or order.
ex: The film's success led to several subsequent sequels.
這部電影的成功帶動了隨後幾部續集。

en: A fee for using a road or bridge; or the number of deaths or damage caused by something; or the sound of a bell.
ex: The death toll from the earthquake has risen to fifty.
地震死亡人數已上升到五十人。

en: Extremely important because everything else depends on it.
ex: Teamwork is crucial to the success of the project.
團隊合作對專案的成功至關重要。

en: To make someone feel very sad; or to reduce the level or value of something.
ex: The long winter always depresses me.
漫長的冬天總讓我心情低落。

en: A large artificial lake used to store water; or a large supply of something.
ex: Water levels in the reservoir are very low this year.
今年水庫的水位非常低。

en: To grow strongly and be healthy or successful.
ex: Plants thrive in warm and sunny places.
植物在溫暖多陽光的地方長得很好。

en: A brown metal made from copper and tin; or a medal for third place.
ex: She won the bronze medal in the 100-meter race.
她在一百公尺賽跑中獲得銅牌。

en: The feeling of being hopeful about the future and expecting good things to happen.
ex: There is cautious optimism about the economy.
人們對經濟抱持謹慎的樂觀。

en: The scientific study of genes and how features are passed from parents to children.
ex: Advances in genetics have changed modern medicine.
遺傳學的進展改變了現代醫學。

en: A person whose job is to study and explain information carefully, or a psychoanalyst.
ex: Analysts expect the company's profits to rise next year.
分析師預期公司明年的利潤會成長。
